newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-UNITED FACE TOUGH TASK AGAINST ARSENAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UNITED FACE TOUGH TASK AGAINST ARSENAL.

text.p: It is many years since a visiting team went to Old Trafford as favourites to beat Manchester United, but that is the position Arsenal find themselves in this weekend. The north London side have overcome their early-season problems and look good enough to sustain a challenge for the title, one that would be reinforced if they sent United crashing to their fifth defeat in six games on Saturday. After being the dominant force in England for much of the last four seasons, Alex Ferguson's team have lost their way recently, beaten 5-0 by Newcastle, 6-3 by Southampton, and 2-1 by Chelsea in the league, as well as conceding their 40-year-old unbeaten European home record to Fenerbahce of Turkey. They have slipped to sixth in the table, eight points behind leaders Newcastle and three behind second-placed Arsenal who have looked confident and hard to beat since Frenchman Arsene Wenger took over at Highbury at the end of September.

Arsenal's 5-2 league cup win over Stoke on Wednesday was their seventh game without loss. With striker Ian Wright in superb form, they could well extend that run against a United team who will be without the suspended Roy Keane in midfield and with confidence at a low ebb.
Wright has scored 15 goals this season -- seven in the last six matches -- and is fast closing in on Cliff Bastin's 60-year-old Arsenal club scoring record of 179 goals set in the 1930s.

Wright, 33, is currently playing as well as ever, has been recalled to the England team and is only 20 goals shy of Bastin's record. And he summed up his new mood this week when he said: "The new manager told me to channel myself into scoring goals and stop complaining to referees, so now I am playing with a smile on my face and it is working wonders. "I do not spend time thinking about breaking the record, it is more important for me to win something this season with Arsenal than break the record. It is no good scoring if it does not bear fruit."
While Frenchman Wenger -- despite unfounded scurrilous stories about his private life -- is on a high with the Gunners, his compatriot Eric Cantona is currently on a low at United.

Cantona's form has been way below his best this season and he needs to re-discover the touch that helped United to win the cup and league double last season if United are to stay in touch with the leaders.
While United will be without Keane on Saturday, they welcome back Ryan Giggs for his first senior match since the end of September.
The United-Arsenal match is one of the top fixtures of the season and United go into it under intense pressure to come out of it with three points.
In the form Arsenal are currently in, United will do well to avoid a further setback.
